messages.content: What's the name of a type of cell that has multiple nuclei?

function.name: bloodcell_classification
function.description: Identify and categorize different types of blood cells based on given attributes. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

cell_shape.description: The shape of the cell, e.g. round, oval.

cell_size.description: The size of the cell, e.g. large, medium, small.

cell_function.description: The function of the cell, e.g. carrying oxygen, fighting infection. Default: 'carry oxygen'.

message.content:
A common example of a cell that contains more than one nucleus is a **multinucleated giant cell** (often called a “giant cell”). These cells arise when several individual cells fuse together, forming a single large cell that carries multiple nuclei within its cytoplasm.

In addition to giant cells, another well‑known category of multinucleated cells is the **syncytium**—a term used broadly to describe any multinucleated cell or tissue that results from the fusion of multiple precursor cells. Classic examples include:

| Cell Type | Origin | Typical Function |
|-----------|--------|------------------|
| Skeletal muscle fiber | Fusion of myoblasts | Contractile movement |
| Syncytiotrophoblast | Fusion of trophoblast cells | Nutrient exchange between mother and fetus |
| Osteoclast | Fusion of monocytes/macrophages | Bone resorption |

So if you’re looking for a specific name, “multinucleated giant cell” is a precise term; otherwise, “syncytium” covers the broader concept of a multinucleated cell.
